topics.chapterTitle: Appendix C — Generic Arithmetic and Range-Lifetime Labs
topics.title: Requirement and simplest approach
topics.summary: Sum a read-only sequence of integer values. Empty input produces zero. Every intermediate addition must be representable in the selected type, or the operation rejects it without modifying caller-owned input. Boolean and floating-point arguments are outside this particular API’s domain. A generic signature must communicate those restrictions without pretending that a concept proves the arithmetic safe.

blocks.text: The unsafe shortcut adds first and checks the result afterward. For signed overflow, that can already have left the language’s defined behavior. The reference compares against safe thresholds before addition. For unsigned values, it checks whether the right operand exceeds the remaining room below the maximum. For signed values, it handles positive and negative right operands separately so the threshold expressions remain representable.

topics.chapterTitle: Appendix C — Generic Arithmetic and Range-Lifetime Labs
topics.title: Evidence and interpretation
topics.summary: The concept expresses a compile-time category: integral types except Boolean. The runtime checks express value-dependent representability. These responsibilities are different. An integer type can satisfy the concept while two values of that type cannot be added safely. Conversely, a floating-point value that happens to be exactly integral remains outside the declared type domain.

blocks.text: The concept expresses a compile-time category: integral types except Boolean. The runtime checks express value-dependent representability. These responsibilities are different. An integer type can satisfy the concept while two values of that type cannot be added safely. Conversely, a floating-point value that happens to be exactly integral remains outside the declared type domain.
rich: The concept expresses a compile-time category: integral types except Boolean. The runtime checks express value-dependent representability. These responsibilities are different. An integer type can satisfy the concept while two values of that type cannot be added safely. Conversely, a floating-point value that happens to be exactly integral remains outside the declared type domain.

blocks.text: The boundary cases include maximum plus zero, minimum plus zero, one step inward from each bound, and one step beyond each bound. A multi-element total fails late enough to demonstrate that earlier local progress does not mutate the caller’s vector. The total is held in local state and returned only after all additions succeed.

blocks.text: The nested experiment covers every pair of signed-char inputs from minus forty through forty. Its independent integer oracle computes values only from minus eighty through eighty, which are representable for the selected test. This is an exhaustive test of that small chosen domain, not of every value of every integral type. The many internal checks remain part of one CTest case and should not be advertised as thousands of independent integration tests.

That is a different API and should be named and tested accordingly. Do not silently change this implementation to saturate merely to keep a calculation running; callers may rely on rejection to prevent publishing a misleading total.

topics.title: Guided extension
topics.summary: Add a checked multiplication function for one explicitly chosen integer type. Derive safe preconditions for zero, positive, and negative operands before writing the operation. Pay particular attention to the minimum signed value multiplied or divided by minus one. Build a bounded independent oracle and boundary cases rather than testing the risky expression in order to discover whether it overflows.

topics.chapterTitle: Appendix C — Generic Arithmetic and Range-Lifetime Labs
topics.title: Requirement and model
topics.summary: A function with local input must return an owning selected result. A temporary span over an external array may expose a valid iterator while the array remains alive. A temporary owning vector passed to a ranges search must not yield an ordinary retained iterator through that algorithm’s safe return type. A view used before a source change should not be reused under an assumption that cached membership state automatically resets.

blocks.text: The experiment demonstrates these distinctions through valid executions and static assertions. It does not create a dangling view and dereference it merely to obtain a sanitizer screenshot. A type-level check or a correctly scoped ownership trace is often a better teaching experiment than deliberately invoking undefined behavior.

topics.chapterTitle: Appendix C — Generic Arithmetic and Range-Lifetime Labs
topics.title: Evidence and interpretation
topics.summary: selected_snapshot constructs a local input vector and a lazy pipeline, then materializes the selected squares into an owning vector. Returning that vector does not retain a borrow of the local source. Its values are checked after the function returns, when the source no longer exists. The result’s independence comes from ownership, not from the fact that the pipeline used modern syntax.

blocks.text: The borrowed-range assertions distinguish the span wrapper from an owning vector. The temporary span’s data belongs to a still-live local array in the caller. That valid array lifetime is essential; borrowed-range status would not rescue a span pointing into destroyed storage. The temporary-vector search instead has a dangling result type, making the unsafe retained-iterator use unavailable through that result.

blocks.text: The source-mutation exercise ends the old view’s use before changing membership and constructs a fresh view afterward. Empty input and no-match input are checked separately so traversal does not assume that a begin iterator is dereferenceable.

topics.title: Guided extension
topics.summary: Design two APIs for selecting task titles. One returns an owning vector of strings. The other returns a view intended for immediate use over a caller-owned immutable collection. Write their lifetime contracts side by side. Test the owning result after the input is replaced; consume the borrowed result only within its valid scope. Explain which interface is suitable for queuing work to a later stage and why.
